name: Road Upgrade Brush
summary: Paint over roads or rails, upgrade up to 200 at once: types, bus lane, tram, trees, catenary.
description:
Road Upgrade Brush

Paint over your roads. Press a button. Go make a coffee.

Ever upgraded 80 country roads one click at a time and, around road 41, started questioning your life choices? Same. So I built a brush.

What it does

  • Paint to select. Hold the left mouse button and every road the circle touches gets selected (red). Roads you are about to catch show up light pink first, so no surprises. Roads that already match your settings turn blue.
  • Upgrade up to 200 roads with one press. Pick a road type and add-ons, hit Upgrade, watch the progress bar.
  • Road types: small, medium and large town streets and country roads.
  • Rails mode: the same brush for rail tracks. Switch Roads | Rails in the toolbar, pick simple, standard or high-speed track, and keep, add or remove the catenary. Tracks of other mods (for example the quiet tracks of Station Noise Barriers) are left alone.
  • Add-ons: alley trees, noise barriers, bus lane, tram track (with or without catenary) and the lock that keeps towns from "improving" your road (keep, lock or unlock).
  • Copy a road: middle-click a road and its settings jump into the toolbar.
  • Underground button (or G): switches to the underground view and selects tunnels only.
  • Not stupid: roads that already are the target are left alone (the status line counts them as "unchanged") and not charged. It leaves other players' roads, industry roads and parts of constructions alone, and it ignores stand-alone tram tracks. A road that fails gets two more tries.
  • Pauses the game for you, then puts your game speed back.
  • Demolishes buildings in the way (switch it off in the toolbar if you are the sentimental type).
  • Translated into the 12 other languages of the game (see the limits below).

How to use it

  1. Build menu, then Roads, then the Tools tab: look for the green brush (Road Upgrade Brush). For rails, the rail tools have the Rail Upgrade Brush.
  2. Set the brush size with the Brush radius slider (5 to 200 m) or the keys M (bigger) and N (smaller).
  3. Paint over the roads. Shift + paint removes roads from the selection. Right click or Clear empties it.
  4. Choose the road type and add-ons in the toolbar on the left.
  5. Press Upgrade (or Enter). Changed your mind mid-run? The Clear button turns into Cancel.

Credits (the real heroes)

I wrote the glue. The hard parts are theirs:

  • square17, Bulk Bulldozer: the brush, the selection, the highlight, the toolbar, and a big part of the translations. The whole "paint over stuff and it just works" feeling comes from their work. I only taught it to upgrade instead of destroy.
  • kurowasiichi, Road Upgrade All in One: the road types, the add-on rules (which add-ons fit together), and the option texts, including the Traditional Chinese translation. Its tool (Combined Road Upgrade in the menu) can upgrade many of the town roads with building lots that this brush cannot.

Both are great mods. Go and subscribe to them. This mod works without them, and next to them.

Limitations and known bugs

  • No undo. Paint carefully.
  • 200 roads per press. Paint the next batch and press again. A run takes about half a second per road.
  • You see the cost only after the upgrade, not before. Demolished buildings can add a lot to the cost.
  • Town roads with building lots can fail with "Unexpected parcel on a segment". The brush cannot do those. It leaves them selected. Road Upgrade All in One (Combined Road Upgrade) can upgrade many of them.
  • Some "Collision" roads fail too. Roads blocked by placed assets are handled. Other collisions are not forced.
  • Esc may close the tool after you click Upgrade, because the game gives the key to its own menu. The run then stops. Use Cancel to keep the tool open.
  • No one-way road types. Rails: only the simple, standard and high-speed tracks of the game.
  • Translations: some come from Bulk Bulldozer and Road Upgrade All in One, the rest are machine-made and not checked by native speakers. If a text sounds odd, tell me and I fix it.

Found a bug? Tell me what you did, and attach stdout.txt if you can. Lines that start with [BrushUpgrade] help a lot.
